video_title: Jalen Duren Update: Pistons Still Expect Him Back w/ Omari Sankofa II,

quotes.speaker: Omari Sankofa II
quotes.summary_phrase: Pistons expect Jalen Duren to remain with the team
quotes.excerpt: I think one way or another, Jalen Duren is going to be a Piston.
quotes.quote: I think one way or another, Jalen Duren is going to be a Piston. What remains to be seen is if that is in a boat-tie year row where he takes the extension or if he takes the qualifying offer, which would allow him to become an unrestricted free agent next year. The Pistons have been pretty adamant. As Kings fans, you have been following, probably have some inkling of that they are not going to pursue any sign-and-trades. So the ball is in Duren's court, essentially.

quotes.speaker: Omari Sankofa II
quotes.summary_phrase: Pistons' strategy for Jalen Duren's contract negotiation
quotes.excerpt: The only way that Duren, his agent can get into more money from the Pistons is by taking the qualifying offer.
quotes.quote: At the end of the day, this is negotiation. The only way that Duren, his agent can get into more money from the Pistons is by taking the qualifying offer. There is no other offer on the table. There is no other mechanism that they can use to try to get more money, and the deadline is tomorrow. So that is the maximum window they have to make a decision.

quotes.speaker: Omari Sankofa II
quotes.summary_phrase: Pistons' leverage in contract talks with Jalen Duren
quotes.excerpt: The Pistons understand that they have leverage. No team forced their hand with an offer.
quotes.quote: The Pistons understand that they have leverage. No team forced their hand with an offer, and restricted free agency is just built really to favor the team. It has become a pretty tough environment for a lot of players in that position. We saw four guys last season have similar standoffs as Jalen Duren. Granted, they did not have $200 million on the table like Duren, but the Pistons understand that Duren's options are pretty slim. So it has gotten to this point, Duren is maximizing his leverage, but the Pistons never once top-signaled that they want to trade him. They expect that he will be back.

quotes.speaker: Omari Sankofa II
quotes.summary_phrase: Weight clause was never part of Jalen Duren's contract
quotes.excerpt: The weight clause was never something that was necessarily put on paper.
quotes.quote: My interpretation of the conversations I have had has been that the weight clause was never something that was necessarily put on paper. It was something that was discussed, but ultimately, it is not something that I think is going to be in the contract. As you are negotiating more money, that typically just comes with more stipulations, which the weight clause could have been part of that, but my understanding is that that was never actually put into the actual contract and it was just something that was discussed.

quotes.speaker: Omari Sankofa II
quotes.summary_phrase: Pistons' offseason moves and internal development
quotes.excerpt: The Pistons did address some really big needs. John Collins, Isaiah Stewart, essentially Isaiah Stewart are really good shooters.
quotes.quote: I do not think they botched it. The reality for the Pistons is that they were operating from a position of strength last season where no one expected you to be that good. They did not have the snazziest offseason, I would not rank offseasons across the East, but the Pistons did address some really big needs. John Collins, Isaiah Stewart, essentially Isaiah Stewart are really good shooters, and that was their big weakness on offense last year. You have got guys who are coming back. Cade just turned 25, Duren does not turn 23 until November, Sasser is 24. So I think they are going into the offseason with some flexibility.

quotes.speaker: Kevin Gleason
quotes.summary_phrase: Debating the weight clause as leverage in contract talks
quotes.excerpt: I think some are suggesting again, this was something that Jalen Duren's camp was using as leverage.

text_blocks.speaker: Kevin Gleason
text_blocks.text: I think some are suggesting again, this was something that Jalen Duren's camp was using as leverage. Good.

quotes.speaker: Allen Stiles
quotes.summary_phrase: Hunter Patterson's report on Jalen Duren's future
quotes.excerpt: What seems to have materialized since Monday is the realization that Duren likely will be in a Detroit uniform.

text_blocks.speaker: Kevin Gleason
text_blocks.text: It is interesting that Hunter Patterson wrote today in The Athletic, what seems to have materialized since Monday is the realization that Duren likely will be in a Detroit uniform next season. Anything after next season remains unclear.

text_blocks.speaker: Allen Stiles
text_blocks.text: And I will tell you this much fellas, you know, it is always a cliché we keep things in our building or everything is good inside. I knew that I partly knew that they got John Collins because I was on Omari's X, but to the outside perspective, we are only hearing about Jalen Duren, especially in Sacramento because that is what we care about.

quotes.speaker: Allen Stiles
quotes.summary_phrase: Pistons' offseason acquisitions and draft strategy

text_blocks.speaker: Allen Stiles
text_blocks.text: Yeah, they got John Collins, Torian Prince, Gary Harris, and then they go out and get Abuka Akori, who all he did was move up the draft boards as a point guard that can back up Cade Cunningham. They had a much better offseason than I think it felt like because anybody only wanted to talk about the drama and Jalen Duren.

text_blocks.speaker: Kevin Gleason
text_blocks.text: Jalen Duren to the Kings for now, it is over.

quotes.speaker: Kevin Gleason
quotes.summary_phrase: Kings need to improve defensively to be better

text_blocks.speaker: Kevin Gleason
text_blocks.text: I think there is one simple way they get better. When I used to coach young ladies in basketball, I used to tell them, basketball is a simple game. It is not easy, but it is simple. If they are better defensively, they are going to be a much better team. So again, that is, oh, that is simple, be better defensively, but it is not easy.

text_blocks.speaker: Allen Stiles
text_blocks.text: Definitely not easy. I would say the shooting. If you are going to go defense, I will go offense because that is what I care about. The three-point shooting. Obviously, you have got to defend the three-point shot.

quotes.speaker: Kevin Gleason
quotes.summary_phrase: Bobby Marks on Kings' defensive struggles

text_blocks.speaker: Kevin Gleason
text_blocks.text: This is what Bobby Marks said about the Kings. The offense should improve with Domantas Sabonis, Zach LaVine, Murray, Hunter all healthy. Questions remain on the defensive side. The Kings finished last season in the bottom of every defensive category, including transition points, second-chance points, three-point percentage and points per game allowed.

text_blocks.speaker: Allen Stiles
text_blocks.text: Getting to see DeAndre Hunter on the court, I guess we are throwing Ben Simmons in that conversation as well, but and Precious Achiuwa playing in, you know, playing from Jump Street. Even the DeQuan Plowdens of the world. I know it is going to be, there are a lot of guys getting time.
